title: The Debt Myth That Keeps You Poor

beats.say: At 24% interest, a neglected $3,000 credit card balance takes 183 months to pay off.
beats.visual: A sleek dark room with a single desk lamp illuminating a red billing statement.

beats.say: That's $4,887 in interest alone. It's why everyone says all debt is pure poison.
beats.visual: Close up of a calculator punching in high interest numbers on a matte black desk.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions. The ultra wealthy borrow billions every single day.
beats.visual: A towering glass skyscraper shot from below against a moody twilight sky.

beats.say: They don't use it for consumer junk. They use low interest debt to buy assets.
beats.visual: A hand sliding a polished brass key across a dark wooden conference table.

beats.say: That is productive debt. It makes you richer while consumer debt drains you dry.
beats.visual: A dark coffee shop corner with a glowing laptop screen reflecting off a window.

beats.say: If a $100,000 property is bought with $20,000 down, that is 5x leverage.
beats.visual: An architectural blueprint unrolling on a slate grey table under warm lights.

beats.say: A 20% price rise doubles your down payment before costs and interest.
beats.visual: A silver pen drawing a sharp upward trend line on a dark grid.

beats.say: If your asset yields more than the debt costs, you profit. But if returns drop, leverage magnifies your losses.
beats.visual: A heavy steel scale tilting slowly downward under a single shadow.

beats.say: The rule is simple. Never borrow for things that drop in value.
beats.visual: A pair of hands closing a sleek leather notebook on a minimal desk.

beats.say: Only borrow when the asset generates cash flow higher than the interest rate.
beats.visual: A blurry city street at night with streaks of amber and red taillights.

beats.say: Master this boundary, and debt becomes a tool. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A dark hallway with a single bright doorway at the far end.

beats.say: Because if you don't control leverage, you will always be trapped when...
beats.visual: A close up of a heavy brass door lock clicking shut in slow motion.

caption:
Not all debt is the same. Consumer debt keeps you broke, but productive debt builds empires. Know the difference.

#debtfree #personalfinance #wealthbuilding #moneymindset #financialliteracy
description: The difference between high-interest consumer debt that ruins your finances and low-interest productive debt that builds long-term wealth.
first_comment: What's the best financial lesson you learned the hard way?

facts.claim: $3,000 credit card at 24% APR paying only the minimum (1% + interest, min $25): 183 months (~15 years), $4,887 interest
A $100,000 property bought with $20,000 down is 5x leverage; a 20% price drop ($20,000) wipes out the whole down payment, a 20% rise doubles it (before costs and interest)
